summary: The Materialized View Sync on 29 October 2026 settled the examples in Appendix B of the materialized view spec. The group agreed to simplify them and reuse the existing event_agg_mv SQL plus a new event_agg_30_day_mv, with example 1 representing the PostgreSQL use case and example 2 the Spark and Trino implementations. The two-dimension description is to be replaced by a statement that the spec does not define freshness, and the spec will mention PostgreSQL, Spark and Trino by name. Jan is to research whether a third example is needed for the ETL case where nested materialized views are treated strictly as tables. The spec goes to the dev list after internal consent.

topics.title: Appendix B examples
topics.summary: The group agreed to simplify the Appendix B examples and use the existing event_agg_mv and a new event_agg_30_day_mv SQL. Example 1 represents the PostgreSQL use case and example 2 the Spark and Trino implementations, and the spec will name those three systems. Jan is to research whether an example 3 is needed, where nested materialized views inside a materialized view are treated strictly as tables: the ETL case in which refresh ordering means nested views need no validation on refresh.
decisions: Simplify the Appendix B examples and use the existing event_agg_mv and new event_agg_30_day_mv SQLs.
Example 1 represents the PostgreSQL use case.
Example 2 represents the Spark and Trino implementations.
The spec will be updated to specifically mention PostgreSQL, Spark and Trino.
open_questions: Is an example 3 needed where nested MVs in an MV are treated strictly as tables (the ETL use case)?

topics.title: Freshness description
topics.summary: The description of the two dimensions is to be removed and replaced with a description saying that the spec does not define freshness.

topics.title: Sharing the spec with the dev list

decisions: Share the spec to the dev mailing list after getting internal consent first.
